newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends up, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends up, seen rising.

text.p: Taiwan's overnight interbank rate closed higher on Thursday and dealers expected the rate to continue to rise amid rising liquidity demand ahead of the February 7 Chinese lunar new year.
The overnight interbank rate finished at 5.773 percent against Wednesday's 5.718 close, with the 30-day commercial paper at 5.65-5.75 percent against 5.70-5.75.

Dealers expected money rates to edge higher on Friday, but central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong vowed to provide funds for local businesses to meet the new year money demand after a board meeting on Thursday afternoon.
The central bank has been injecting funds into the banking system through open market operations to help ease liquidity in recent days.
The bond market was quiet in afternoon trade. The 10-year 86/4 bond yield was traded at 6.105 earlier in the session.
